synopsis: ISO 34501–34505 provide road-vehicle scenario vocabulary, ODD specification, categorisation and test-case methods; their structure can inform off-road validation, but their road-specific content is not off-road compliance evidence and acceptance for earth-moving collision avoidance remains uncertain [f7692, f6642, f449, f4315]. No heavy-machinery equivalent of ISO 34502 was found, so the programme must define its own scenario or hazard taxonomy; the booklet adopts functional, logical and concrete scenarios, using ISO 21815 and EMESRT storyboards for off-road content [f9881, f9882, f15323]. ISO 34505:2025, dated June 2025, specifies test-case identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, platform and expected results, while ISO 34503 provides a hierarchical ODD structure whose road-oriented attributes require adaptation [f6732, f6706, f6709]. These standards primarily address coverage rather than model credibility, establish no physical-to-virtual testing ratio, and do not address risk scaling; ISO/PAS 34506 concerns virtual-environment qualification but remained a draft in October 2026 [f7693, f7694, f8119, f4072]. TÜV SÜD nevertheless summarizes ISO 34502 and European automated-driving regulation as requiring the virtual platform itself to be demonstrated fit for purpose, so scenario coverage alone should not be confused with platform qualification [f1283, f7693]. No off-road equivalent of ISO 19206 standardized targets exists in the corpus: its transferable value is target-design principles, with surrogates representing off-road people, vehicles, machines and obstacles and matching each sensor’s relevant response [f15329, f15325, f15326].
